meta.title: Kubernetes Basics
meta.description: Covers core Kubernetes concepts: Pods, Services, Deployments, and ConfigMaps.

questions.text: What is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes?
questions.explanation: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes. It wraps one or more containers that share the same network namespace and storage volumes.
hints: Think about what Kubernetes schedules, not what Docker runs.
It can contain multiple containers that share a network.

questions.text: Which of the following are valid Kubernetes Service types? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The four valid Service types are ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, and ExternalName. 'IngressPort' does not exist — Ingress is a separate resource.
hints: There are exactly four valid types.
One of the options is named after a different resource kind entirely.

questions.text: A Deployment automatically replaces Pods that fail or are evicted.
questions.explanation: A Deployment uses a ReplicaSet under the hood to maintain the desired number of Pod replicas. If a Pod dies, the controller creates a replacement.
hints: Consider what the 'desired state' model means for running replicas.

questions.text: Which resource would you use to store non-sensitive configuration data that Pods can consume as environment variables or mounted files?
questions.explanation: ConfigMaps store non-sensitive key-value pairs and can be injected into Pods as environment variables or volume-mounted files. Secrets are for sensitive data and are base64-encoded.
hints: The name of the resource is a strong hint.
Secrets are its sibling resource — used for passwords, tokens, etc.

questions.text: Drag each Kubernetes resource to the box that best describes its primary purpose.
questions.explanation: Pods run containers, Services expose them over the network, ConfigMaps hold configuration data, and PersistentVolumes provide durable disk storage.
hints: Think about what each resource's name implies about its job.
